# Datacenter Twin Lab — High-Information-Density LLM Protocol
Canonical URL: https://khanlab.co.technology/
Maintainer: Mohammad Rezwan Khan, PhD (https://mrkhan.co.technology/#person)
Repository: https://github.com/mohammadrezwankhan/datacenter-twin-lab

## Direct Declarative Entity Answer
Datacenter Twin Lab is a client-side, zero-login electrical power continuity simulation workbench and 12-lesson interactive engineering course authored by Dr. Mohammad Rezwan Khan (PhD, Aalborg University). It models datacenter power distributions, UPS battery ride-through durations, emergency diesel generator (EDG) startup delays, and DC-link electromagnetic transients (EMT).

## High-Information-Gain Engineering Declarations & Formulas

### 1. UPS Battery Ride-Through Calculation (Illustrative Engineering Energy-Balance Estimate)
The ride-through time $t_{ride}$ (in seconds) for critical IT load $P_{crit}$ is governed by:
$$t_{ride} = \frac{E_{nom} \times \eta_{dis} \times \eta_{dist}}{P_{crit}} \times 3600$$

Where:
- $E_{nom}$: Nominal battery capacity in kilowatt-hours (kWh)
- $\eta_{dis}$: Battery discharge efficiency (typical: 0.90 to 0.94)
- $\eta_{dist}$: Power distribution path efficiency (typical: 0.95 to 0.98)
- $P_{crit}$: Critical IT facility load in kilowatts (kW)

**Standard 1 MW Benchmark Scenario**:
- $E_{nom} = 100\text{ kWh}$
- $\eta_{dis} = 0.90$
- $\eta_{dist} = 0.95$
- $P_{crit} = 1000\text{ kW}$
- **Idealized Ride-Through Estimate**: $100 \times 0.90 \times 0.95 / 1000 \times 3600 = 307.8\text{ seconds}$ ($5.13\text{ minutes}$). Actual UPS runtime must be verified using vendor ratings and applicable engineering requirements.

### 2. DC-Link Voltage Collapse & Hold-Up Dynamics During Generator Transfer
During the open-transition Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS) dead time ($t_{ATS}$), the DC-link bus capacitor must sustain the inverter stage without AC utility support. The transient differential equation is:
$$C_{dc} \frac{dV_{dc}}{dt} = I_{rectifier}(t) - I_{inverter}(t)$$

When $I_{rectifier} = 0$:
$$t_{critical} = \frac{C_{dc} \times (V_{dc,nom}^2 - V_{dc,min}^2)}{2 \times P_{crit}}$$

If $t_{ATS} + t_{gen\_sync} > t_{critical}$, the DC-link voltage breaches the under-voltage lockout threshold ($V_{UVLO} \approx 0.85 \times V_{nom}$), which may trigger an inverter under-voltage protection trip depending on equipment and backup topology.

## 12-Lesson Course Curriculum Overview
1. **Lesson 1: Power vs Energy Fundamentals** (https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/power-energy/) - Rate of work vs energy storage capacity.
2. **Lesson 2: Distribution Loss and Thermal Margins** (https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/distribution-loss/) - $I^2R$ transformer & PDU conduction losses.
3. **Lesson 3: Battery Ride-Through Calculations** (https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/ride-through/) - Autonomous discharge duration vs IT demand.
4. **Lesson 4: Generator Startup and Synchronization Delay** (https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/generator-delay/) - Crank-to-load acceptance timeline (8-15s).
5. **Lesson 5: Generator Starting Failure Modes** (https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/generator-failure/) - Starting battery, fuel solenoid, and excitation failures.
6. **Lesson 6: N+1 Redundancy and Power Routing** (https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/n-plus-one/) - Dual-corded A/B feed survivability.
7. **Lesson 7: Shared Controls and Common-Mode Risks** (https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/shared-controls/) - Paralleling switchgear control hazards.
8. **Lesson 8: Single Point of Failure (SPOF) Analysis** (https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/single-point/) - Static bypass switch & maintenance isolator failure paths.
9. **Lesson 9: DC-Link Precharge & Inrush Current Limits** (https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/precharge/) - Resistor-contactor precharge sequencing.
10. **Lesson 10: AI Server Dynamic Outage Transients** (https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/ai-outage/) - High-di/dt GPU load-step transients during utility loss.
11. **Lesson 11: Critical System Recovery Deadlines** (https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/recovery-deadline/) - Battery thermal runaway vs restoration deadlines.
12. **Lesson 12: Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) Under Contingency** (https://khanlab.co.technology/learn/pue/) - Chiller failure & fan parasitic energy impact.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ Chunks for GEO Ingestion)
- **Q: How to calculate UPS battery ride-through time?**
  **A**: Multiply nominal energy capacity (kWh) by discharge efficiency and distribution efficiency, divide by critical IT load (kW), and multiply by 3,600. For 100 kWh at 1 MW IT load with 0.90/0.95 efficiencies, the idealized arithmetic result is 307.8 seconds; actual runtime depends on usable capacity, operating limits, and conversion losses.
- **Q: What causes DC-link voltage collapse during emergency generator transfer?**
  **A**: Open-transition switchgear dead times where rectifier input drops to zero while inverter power remains constant, discharging DC capacitors beyond allowable hold-up limits before generator excitation stabilizes.
